description_full: Youdao, Inc., an internet technology company, provides online services in the fields of content, community, communication, and commerce in the People's Republic of China. It operates through three segments: Learning Services, Smart Devices, and Online Marketing Services. The Learning Services segment offers digital content services, which provides interactive learning features, such as Youdao Lingshi; STEAM courses, including Youdao iCode operated by Youdao Premium Courses; and adult courses comprising China University MOOC. The Smart Devices segment develops and offers smart devices, such as Youdao Dictionary Pen, Youdao Tutoring Pen, and Youdao Smart Learning Terminal. The Online Marketing Services Segment provides performance-based advertising, and global marketing and promotion services. It also offers Youdao Dictionary, a language app; other dictionary and translation tools; and AI-based learning tools, including Hi Echo, Mr. P AI Tutor and Scholar AI by Confucius LLM. In addition, the company licenses technologies and services through Youdao Smart Cloud. It provides learning content, applications, and solutions, which cover topics and target people from age groups through its websites and mobile applications. Youdao, Inc. was founded in 2006 and is headquartered in Hangzhou, China. Youdao, Inc. operates as a subsidiary of NetEase, Inc.

financial_summary: Youdao, Inc. is a mid-cap consumer defensive business with a $2.4B market cap on $887M of annual revenue.

The top line has compounded at +76% over the past three years, the kind of sustained demand persistence that marks a compounder. Operating margins are expanding by +8.3pp year-over-year, which is one of the strongest signals that the moat is deepening.
Returns on capital run at -11078% against a 9% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, with gross margins sitting at 49%.

The business throws off $4M in free cash flow — roughly 1 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders. Cash conversion is thin at 0.51×, however, which raises the oldest question in analysis: are these earnings backed by cash?.
On the balance sheet, the balance sheet carries net cash, which is the gold standard: the business never has to make desperate decisions in a bad year, and interest coverage runs at 3.5×.

Shareholder yield is only 0.0%, a thin return of capital, and insiders hold 14% of the shares, so management thinks like owners because it is one — the strongest alignment there is, and profit capture is only 0.5× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
